Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:3: And he said further, of blessed memory: upon the brain rests blessing, upon the heart rests holiness, upon the lung rests unity, and thought comprises them all - and these are "the LORD bless you," "the LORD shine," "the LORD lift up" - "the LORD bless you" in the brain, "shine" in the heart, where the light of the eyes is, "lift up" in the lung, which is peace - this is what is written, "and give you peace" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:4: Behold, it is explained in the teaching that holiness is in the heart, and the reason for this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Shelach, page 161a), that a person is the pattern of a small world, and there is in man an allusion to the world, to the Temple and the Holy of Holies, and he said that the heart corresponds to the Holy of Holies, in these words: come and see, when the Holy One, blessed be He, created a person in the world, He arranged him in a precious supernal manner, and gave him his strength and power in the middle of the body, where the heart rests, which is the strength and sustenance of the whole body, and from there the whole body is nourished, and all the limbs of the body are nourished from there - and behold, the heart takes hold and grasps the supernal place above, which is the brain of the head that rests above, and takes hold of it, and this is bound to that. In this manner the Holy One, blessed be He, arranged and made him one body, and arranged the limbs of the body around the heart, and the heart rests in the middle, and the whole body and all the limbs are nourished from that heart, which is the strength of all, and everything depends on it, and that heart is bound and attached to the supernal brain that rests above. So it is: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He arranged the sea, the ocean, that surrounds all the inhabited world, and the inhabited world of all seventy nations all surrounds Jerusalem, and Jerusalem rests in the middle of all the inhabited world, and it surrounds the Temple Mount, and the Temple Mount surrounds the courtyards of Israel, and those courtyards surround the Chamber of Hewn Stone where the Great Sanhedrin sits, and we have learned there is no sitting in the courtyard except for the kings of the House of David alone, and the Chamber of Hewn Stone surrounds the House of the Portico, and the Portico [surrounds] the altar, and the altar surrounds the Sanctuary, and the Sanctuary [surrounds] the House of the Holy of Holies, where the Shechinah rests, and the cover, and the cherubim, and the ark - and here is the heart of the whole land and world, and from here all those inhabited places, which are the limbs of the body, are nourished, and the heart is nourished from the brain of the head, and this is attached to that - this is what is written (Exodus 15:17), "the place You made for Your dwelling" - in this manner higher and higher, and so on - to this point, relevant here. And further there, he explained in the teaching that all these aspects, of this world and of the Temple, are also above, and higher and higher - and it is not for our discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:5: And it emerges from this, for our intent, that the heart in a person corresponds to the House of the Holy of Holies, in which are the ark, the cover, and the cherubim - and we learn from this that just as in the Temple the Shechinah rested there because the ark, tablets, and cherubim were there, and so on, so too the heart of a person should be made ready that the Shechinah rest in it and that it be a holy of holies. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (page 140b), that concerning the wings of the lung it is said (Exodus 25:20), "and the cherubim shall spread their wings above, covering with their wings over the cover [kapporet]," and they said, of blessed memory, "over the cover" - this is the atonement [kapparah] of the heart; "the holy of holies" - this is the heart - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:6: And there (page 13b) another aspect concerning the heart is explained, and it says that the ark that was in the Tabernacle corresponded to the heart, in these words: the ark is certainly the heart, and the lamp burning is comprised of the thirty-two paths, and it is the Sabbath, and in it is the supernal Shechinah, which is the Torah of the wise, and with it the heart understands. And it says further there, "the atonement of the heart" is the spreading of the tabernacle of peace, of which it is said, "He who spreads the tabernacle of peace" - to this point. And the intent is that the ark corresponds to the heart, which is the Shechinah comprised of the thirty-two paths, for the heart is the Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 49b), where it says, "a heart that understands, a heart that knows, a heart that sees" is the Shechinah, and so on. And so too in the Tikkunim, in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 114b), concerning "let us make man," they counted nine limbs, and said there, "let us make man" - this is the heart, that it be the completion of everything - the intent being that it is the tenth aspect, corresponding to the Shechinah, as expounded there concerning the other limbs. And they said, "the heart understands" - the intent being that the supernal Shechinah bestows upon it the power of understanding, that the heart understand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:7: And in Tikkun 25 (Tikkunim, page 70a), he says that the five wings of the lung, with the "rosette," which are six, correspond to the seraphim, of whom it is said (Isaiah 6:2), "each had six wings, six wings" - and he says the six are from the side of the letter Vav, which is the Torah scroll, and the ark of the Torah scroll is the seat of the heart, and it is a burning fire - and were it not for the wings of the lung that fan upon it, the heart would burn up the whole body, and that fire, which is the blood of the heart's vessels, the spirit fans the vessels of blood, and they are all led by it - this is what is written (Ezekiel 1:12), "to wherever the spirit would go, they went" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:8: And this spirit that cools the blood of judgment is from the side of Tiferet, who is the master of mercy - and so he explained further there: and when the spirit comes to the heart, where the nefesh is, of it is said (Song of Songs 5:2), "the voice of my beloved knocks."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:9: And so it is further explained in the Tikkunim (page 53a), in these words: this spirit, in every place where the supernal and lower Shechinah is found, is the Vav that blows in the wings of the lung, and upon the heart, where the lamp of the LORD is, this is the soul in the brain, spirit in the wings of the lung, nefesh in the heart. And sometimes three in three brains, and thought rides upon them, which is Adam. And so three for the heart: "ner" [lamp] - neshamah, ru'ach, that blows into them, "ner," in the two chambers of the heart, which are nefesh and ru'ach, the sign "ner." And this Vav is what blows in the arms, in their six joints, and it blows in the two legs, which are (Song of Songs 5:15), "his legs are pillars of marble" - and concerning it is said (Isaiah 11:2), "and the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him" - when the limbs of the body conduct themselves with this spirit through the precepts of the Torah, the ship is steered to every direction a person wishes, as it is said (Ezekiel 1:12), "to wherever the spirit would go, they went" - for the ship is the head, and it is the heart, and it is the body. And if the ten limbs of the body, which are the masters of the ship, which are the holy people, do not conduct themselves with Torah, which is the neshamah, with the commandment, which is the nefesh, the spirit flies away from among them, and at that time (Jonah 1:4), "and the LORD hurled a great wind [spirit] into the sea," which is a stormy wind - the harsh decree of judgment that storms the body of the person, who is Israel, and Israel are in the storm, and the ship, which is the body, was about to break - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:10: And at the beginning of the teaching he explained that neshamah, ru'ach, nefesh have their dwellings: neshamah in the brain, ru'ach in the wings of the lung, nefesh in the heart. And so he also explained in the Tikkunim (page 49a), in these words: and further, a person's neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh are teruah, tekiah, shevarim - nefesh in the heart, and this is shevarim, as it is said (Psalms 51:19), "a broken and crushed heart"; neshamah in the brain, and this is tekiah; ru'ach in the wings of the lung that blows upon the heart, and this is teruah, and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:11: And what is relevant from this matter in practice is explained in the teaching: that when one is occupied with Torah and commandments, this spirit spreads through the whole body, for this spirit is the inwardness of Da'at, the soul that spreads within the six extremities, and this is (Ezekiel 1:12), "to wherever the spirit would go, they went." And if not, Heaven forfend, this holy spirit withdraws, and a stormy wind rules, which is harsh judgment, and then "the ship was about to break."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:12: Further, he said in the Tikkunim (end of page 140b), in these words: nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah - priest, Levite, and Israelite. The priest is neshamah - if he merits it, "the lamp of the LORD," the lamp shone within it from the heart like a shining sun, and a holy spirit would go out from between the wings of the cherubim, which are the wings of the lung, and it speaks with him. And if not, fire - this is nefesh - fire would go out from the heart and burn him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:13: And similarly to this they explained further there, before this, in these words: the kidneys are advisers - if they merit it, prophecy enters them, which is "the lamp of the LORD, the soul of man," and they become prophets and advise for good, and there is in them counsel and sound wisdom. The wings of the lung, if they merit it, the holy spirit rests in them, and of them it is said (Isaiah 11:2), "and the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and fear of the LORD," and concerning them it is said (Exodus 25:20), "and the cherubim shall spread their wings," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:14: And relevant to the holiness of the heart are two aspects, one positive and one negative. The positive aspect is that, since the nefesh's place is in the heart, as explained in the teachings we copied, the holiness of the nefesh is the holiness of performing the commandments, as we explained above in chapter 4, and we copied the wording of Rashbi (Tikkunei Zohar, page 68b), who said, "I have made it" - this is the nefesh, where the performance rests, resting in the two hundred forty-eight precepts. And this matter the verse is precise about, in saying (Numbers 15:39), "and you shall not go about after your heart," and so on, "so that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy," and so on - it appears that the repair of the heart is through the performance of the commandments, and through this it is sanctified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:15: Further, we learn from the words of Rashbi, who said that the pouch of the heart is the ark, and it is known (Bava Batra 14b) that inside the ark were the tablets and the fragments of the tablets - so it is fitting that his heart be full of Torah, and the spirit that blows from the wings of the lung, which is Vav, should blow into it the light of the atmosphere of Torah properly, and he shall merit the holy spirit like the virtue of the High Priest, as explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:16: And corresponding to the fragments of the tablets, his heart must be a broken and crushed heart, to be a preparation for the Shechinah, for the Shechinah's dwelling is among her broken vessels, as explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, page 9a), and these are the poor whose heart is broken and crushed. And whoever's heart is proud pushes the Shechinah away from him (Proverbs 16:5), as it is said, "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD" - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (page 69b), in these words: the pride of a heart that is complete with its husks and not broken, of it is said, "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD," and the Shechinah does not rest upon him - to this point. And in the Gate of Fear, chapter 4, we copied his entire wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:17: And without doubt, even the nefesh that rests in the heart shall withdraw, since he brings into the heart a husk that pushes it away, for holiness does not rest in a place where there is an external force - "evil shall not sojourn with You" - and the proof is that when they brought an image into the Sanctuary, the Shechinah withdrew. And so every blemish a person causes in his heart through envy, hatred, anger, and rivalry is like bringing an image into the Sanctuary of the Holy of Holies, since it has already been explained that the heart is the Holy of Holies - and this is the negative aspect, that one must guard against all these, so that his heart be a holy vessel in which the Shechinah rests, and the Shechinah not find, Heaven forfend, any blemish of an external force that would push her away.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:18: And just as we are warned on the Sabbath day against anger and sadness, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24, page 69b), so one must be careful during the six days of the week - this is the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Tikkun 48 (page 85a): happy is he who guards the dwelling for the Sabbath, which is the heart, that the sadness of the spleen and the anger of the gall bladder, which is the fire of Gehinnom, not draw near there - of it is said (Exodus 35:3), "you shall not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day" - and this is certainly so, that whoever becomes angry is as though he kindled the fire of Gehinnom - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:19: And certainly we need this warning always - both not to become angry even on a weekday, so as not to kindle the fire of Gehinnom, but on the Sabbath day the blemish is without limit, for since the fire of Gehinnom is completely nullified and this one kindles it anew, his punishment is very great. And on the Sabbath day a person must be slow to anger and be exceedingly humble, and learn from the attributes of his Maker, that on the Sabbath day He is patient with the wicked in Gehinnom, whose fire is nullified - and as explained in Parashat Yitro (page 89a), because Atika is revealed, all wraths and all judgments are stilled on the Sabbath day, and how many idol-worshippers are before Him, and He is patient. And from the attribute of humility that he acquires on the Sabbath day he shall draw upon all six days, for the Sabbath day is the root of all holinesses, as we explained in chapter 2, and shall further be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:20: And so, just as one must guard himself from sadness of heart [on the Sabbath], so must he on weekdays, for the Shechinah does not rest through sadness, and so on, but through joy, as explained in the Talmud (Shabbat 30b) - except at times when sadness is needed, such as the four fasts on which one fasts for the destruction of the Temple, when even before Him there is sadness, as explained in the Talmud (Chagigah 13a), that in the inner chambers there is sadness; and so they said in Tractate Berachot, first chapter (3a), the night has three watches, and over each watch the Holy One, blessed be He, and so on, as explained there - at these times sadness is good. Or if he is sad over his sins, none of this is a blemish in the heart - but sadness that comes from the affairs of this world is what blemishes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:21: And his inside must be like his outside, and its secret is explained in the Tikkunim (page 128b), in these words: whoever is from the Tree of Life, his inside is like his outside, mouth and heart equal, and concerning them it is said (Genesis 3:22), "and take also from the Tree of Life and eat, and live forever." But another, whose mouth and heart are not equal, of him it is said, "and from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil you shall not eat of it" - for he is certainly an evil mixture that counterfeits the King's coin, that mixes silver with lead, and so on - to this point, relevant here, to be explained further in its secret concerning the matter of prayer, God willing. And he must speak truth in his heart, for through this he causes the unification of the attribute of truth in the heart, and this is the secret of (Psalms 85:12), "truth shall spring up from the earth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:22: And the general rule is that since the heart is the source of life, placed in the middle of the body, and corresponds to the House of the Holy of Holies, which is the central point of the world, all the good qualities in the limbs flow from the heart, and likewise the opposite - and therefore they said in Tractate Avot (chapter 2, mishnah 9), in the mishnah of the five disciples of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: Rabbi Eliezer says, a good eye, and so on; Rabbi Elazar says, a good heart - and he said, I see the words of Elazar ben Arach as superior to your words, for his words include your words. And likewise the opposite: an evil heart is the root of all repugnant qualities.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:23: Further, they said in the Talmud, Nedarim (20b), and the Yalkut (remez 750), in explaining the verse (Numbers 15:39), "and you shall not go about after your heart" - from here Rabbi Natan said, a person should not drink from one cup and set his eye on another cup. Rava said, this was necessary only [to teach it applies] even to his two [own] wives. Another interpretation: "and you shall not go about after your heart and after your eyes" - this teaches that the eyes follow the heart, or does the heart follow the eyes? You might say - but is there not a blind man who commits all the abominations of the world? Rather, what does Scripture teach by "and you shall not go about after your heart"? This teaches that the eyes follow the heart. And he says further there, Rabbi Yitzchak said, the heart and the eye are two brokers of sin, "and you shall not go about," and so on. "Give Me your heart, my son, and let your eyes observe My ways" (Proverbs 23:26) - the Holy One, blessed be He, said, if you give Me your heart and your eye, I know that you are Mine - to this point. Behold, it is explained that the heart is the source of all qualities, whether for good or the opposite, and therefore the verse places the heart before the eyes, "and you shall not go about after your heart" and afterward "and after your eyes," and likewise, "give Me your heart, my son, and your eyes," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:24: And according to the view of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, who said, "if you give Me your heart and your eye," it must be said that the plain sense of the verse is, "give Me your heart, my son" - and here the accent breaks the verse - "and let your eyes observe My ways" - and the reason Scripture did not say, "give Me your heart and your eyes," together, is because the heart is the essential thing, as explained in the teaching that says the eyes follow the heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:25: Thus far we have spoken of what is relevant to the particulars of the heart. However, concerning what is relevant to the generalities of the holiness of thoughts that depend on the two things mentioned, the brain and the heart, there are further particulars alluded to in Scripture and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, which are essential to the holiness of thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:26: The first of them is that one should constantly rise every night at midnight and occupy himself with Torah until daylight. And in the property of rising at midnight to occupy oneself with Torah there are great virtues, to be explained, with God's help, one of them being the subduing of the husks - and this matter is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 242a), on the verse (Genesis 49:14), "Issachar is a strong-boned donkey" - he opened and said (Psalms 27:1), "the LORD is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear; the LORD is the stronghold of my life, of whom shall I be afraid" - how beloved are the words of Torah, how beloved are those who strive in Torah before the Holy One, blessed be He, for whoever strives in Torah does not fear the mishaps of the world - he is guarded above, guarded below, and not only that, but he subdues all the mishaps of the world and brings them down to the depths of the great abyss.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:27: Come and see, when night enters, closed gates open, and dogs and donkeys are set loose and roam the world, and permission is given to destroy, and all the people of the world lie on their beds, and the souls of the righteous ascend to delight above. When the north wind is aroused and the night is divided, a holy arousal is aroused in the world, and it is said in several places, happy is the portion of that person who stands at that hour and strives in Torah - for once he opens with Torah, he brings all those evil kinds down into the holes of the great abyss, and subdues the donkey and brings it down among the officers beneath the dust of filthy dung. Therefore Issachar, whose striving was in Torah, subdued the donkey, and brought it down from that "strong-boned" one who rises to harm the world, and set its dwelling "between the sheepfolds," among the filth of the dusty officers - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:28: And we have already elaborated above that the confusion of thoughts that comes to a person while standing in prayer or while occupied with Torah is because of his sins, which make him unfit to unify - and the sin is the external accuser that comes between him and his God. And since this person is accustomed to rise at midnight to occupy himself with Torah, he subdues the Other Side, and his sins are atoned for, and through this he comes to purify his thought and his unification is not confused.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:29: And the reason for this, it is possible to say, is because the attribute of night is what bestows the judgments, and from it the external forces draw the judgments, and it is transformed from darkness to light - meaning from the attribute of judgment to the attribute of mercy - through the occupation with Torah, and since it is sweetened, all those that depend on it are likewise sweetened. And further, because the harshest husk of all the husks is death, and sleep is one-sixtieth of death (Berachot 57b), and since a person banishes sleep from his eyes, the harshest husk is found to be broken, and of itself certainly all the rest are subdued and broken, and the light of the pupil of the eye shines through the light of Torah. And therefore King David, peace be upon him, would not sleep at night more than sixty breaths (Sukkah 26b; Zohar, Parashat Vayigash, page 207a), for the reason stated - and so every penitent must banish sleep from his eyes at night through the occupation with Torah and prayer, in order to subdue the husks, and it will certainly be of great assistance to his repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:30: And so they said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 50, page 86b): and all this is provided for according to the deeds of people - happy is he who raises it to its place and the Holy One, blessed be He, to His place, of whom it is said (Isaiah 19:1), "behold, the LORD rides upon a swift cloud"; "behold, the LORD goes forth from His place" (ibid. 26:21). Rabbi Elazar said to him, Father, can a person truly restore the Holy One, blessed be He, to His place? Yes - as I found concerning David, who said (Psalms 132:4), "if I give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids, until I find a place for the LORD," and so on - at the time a person restores Him to His place, what is written of him? "From His place He shall turn in mercy to His people," and so on - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that King David, peace be upon him, by banishing sleep from his eyes, restored the Holy One, blessed be He, to His place - and from him every individual shall learn, that since through his sin he causes the exile of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah from His place, as explained in the Gate of Fear, it is fitting that he repent and banish sleep from his eyes, to restore them to their place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:31: And so, when a person considers that after his death his eyes are closed from seeing, how he will then regret the past and say, while my eyes were open, why did I not look through them at the occupation with Torah and banish sleep from my eyes - therefore, while the spirit of life is still within him, he should distance himself from death and cleave to Torah, which is the Tree of Life, along the lines of what is said in the Zohar, Parashat Naso (page 126a), in the teaching on (Psalms 104:1), "bless the LORD, O my soul," which we copied in the Gate of Fear, chapter 12, at the end of the teaching: when David considered those judgments a person [faces] when he departs from this world, he anticipated and said, "bless the LORD, O my soul," before you leave the world - now, while you are partnered with the body, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:32: Further, there is also a proof in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 12b) that rising at midnight aids the purification of thoughts - it says there that the psalm (Psalms 134:1), "behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD," is said of those who stand to occupy themselves with Torah at midnight, and it says, who are those whose praise is entirely for the King? It continues and says, "who stand in the house of the LORD by night" - these are called servants of the LORD, these are fit to bless the King, and their blessing is a [true] blessing - this is what is written (Psalms 134:2), "lift up your hands in holiness and bless the LORD" - you are found fit for the holy King to be blessed through your hands, and the blessing that is through your hands is a [true] blessing - to this point. And since it says that the supernal King is blessed through him, certainly his thoughts are correct and clean - and when he is confused and not in [proper] thought, his blessing is not a [true] blessing and his unification is not a [true] unification - but certainly Heaven assists him to become completely righteous and for his thought to be holy, and this is among the virtues of one who rises at midnight to occupy himself with Torah, which is explained in Parashat Vayikra: that the Torah informs him of his sin so that he repent - so he explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 23b), on the verse (Leviticus 4:23), "or if his sin is made known to him," in these words: and whoever stands at night to labor in Torah, the Torah informs him of his sin, not in the manner of judgment but like a mother who informs her son with soft words, and he does not forget it and repents before his Master. And should you say, David, who rose at midnight, why was he aroused against in judgment? Rather, David was different, for he transgressed in what he was bound to, and sought judgment, and by what he transgressed he was judged - he sinned against the holy kingship, and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:33: There is further proof for this matter from the teaching we copied in Parashat Vayikra (ibid., page 13a), which says further there, that concerning the servants of the LORD mentioned it is said, "lift up your hands in holiness and bless the LORD," and it is explained there that this is the secret of the supernal Chokhmah, which is the "Eden" called "holy [kodesh]." And certainly, if there is no attachment in his soul to the place of holiness, he cannot draw a blessing from there for the LORD - but certainly he is first sanctified from there, and through this he can afterward draw a blessing from there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:34: And so it is explained in the Zohar (ibid., Parashat Lech Lecha, page 92b), that one who stands to occupy himself with Torah draws from the "stream of the ancients," in these words: Rabbi Chizkiyah said, whoever strives at this hour certainly has a portion forever in the World to Come. Rabbi Yosi said, why "forever"? He said to him, so I have learned - that every midnight, when the Holy One, blessed be He, is aroused in the Garden of Eden, all the plantings of the garden are watered more from that stream called "the stream of the ancients," "the stream of delights," whose waters never cease - as it were, that one who stands and strives in Torah, it is as though that stream is poured upon his head and waters him among those plantings of the Garden of Eden. Rabbi Yosi said, since all the righteous in the Garden of Eden heed him, they give him a portion in that watering of the stream, so he is found to have a portion forever in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:35: And when you examine what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 88a) concerning "the stream of the ancients, the stream of delights," it will not seem far that his thought becomes sanctified, for he draws from the holy [source], since that stream is poured upon his head, and therefore he can draw a blessing from there - and it is fitting that the thought resting in his head become sanctified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:36: However, in order to merit being holy with the holiness of thought as explained, his Torah must be a clean Torah - for if he is wicked, his Torah is despised, as it is written (Psalms 50:16), "and to the wicked, God said, what have you to do with declaring My statutes" - and it cannot be said of him that the righteous place his portion in that watering of the stream, for by his deeds he is pushed away from there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:37: And further, what the teaching says, that he is called a servant of the LORD - "behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD, who stand in the house of the LORD by night" (ibid. 134:1) - and the intent of "who stand in the house of the LORD by night" is explained to mean that his image stands above, engraved in the Shechinah, which is the house of the LORD, which says, "see with what I am aroused toward you" (Zohar, Parashat Vayikra, page 13a). For it cannot be said that "stand in the house of the LORD" means specifically that a person studies in the synagogue, which is the house of the LORD - for we find several stories in the Zohar of the colleagues of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who studied at night in their homes, and especially when they were exiled outside their homes and studied in caves and villages, particularly in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 92) in the story of the village of Tarsha, where their study was at midnight in the guest house. Rather, certainly the correct explanation is as we explained, that he stands "in the house of the LORD," meaning that he merited through his deeds that his image is engraved above in the house of the LORD. And if he is wicked, his image is erased from the house of the LORD, and even though he occupies himself with Torah, his Torah effects no arousal. And therefore, whoever wishes to merit this measure must be a complete penitent, and then Heaven will assist him so that his image be engraved above, to be called a servant of the LORD, and to draw from the holy [source], and the other virtues explained and to be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:38: And among the conditions of a penitent is that he rise at night to confess and weep over his sins, as elaborated by the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot, peace be upon him. And so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:147), "I rose before dawn and cried out," and so on, and he said (ibid. 119:55), "I remembered Your Name, O LORD, in the night, and kept Your Torah" - and the intent is that because, being at night, he remembers His blessed Name in songs and praises, this is the cause of "and kept Your Torah," and as explained above, that rising at midnight subdues the Other Side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:39: And this is what he says right afterward (ibid. 119:56), "this I had, because I kept Your precepts" - by the plain meaning it says, this measure mentioned, that I would remember His blessed Name at night, this is what caused me "that I kept Your precepts." And by way of secret, because one who rises at night joins with "this" [zot], which is the Shechinah, and since he joins with her, the Shechinah does not allow him to be pushed away from her and for the evil inclination to rule over him to cause him to sin - since he wishes to be among the servants of the LORD, one who comes to purify himself is assisted, and this is "because I kept Your precepts," along the lines stated. And so he also said (Psalms 88:2), "O LORD, God of my salvation, I have cried out by day, and in the night before You" - and "my salvation," the explanation is essentially to save me from the hand of the evil inclination, as explained in the Zohar. If so, it is fitting for every penitent who rises at night to occupy himself with Torah, that he first confess and weep over his sins, and afterward Heaven will assist him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:40: Now, besides the aspect of the holiness of thought that depends on rising at midnight, as we explained, there is in rising at midnight a general holy aspect for a Torah scholar, which is relevant to the topic of this Gate we are engaged in - and this aspect is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 81a), in these words: Rabbi Abba said, why are the passage of forbidden relations and the passage "you shall be holy" adjacent to each other? Rather, so we have learned: whoever guards himself from these forbidden relations is certainly made holy, and all the more so if he sanctifies himself with the holiness of his Master - and the colleagues have already aroused themselves as to when is everyone's time to be sanctified. Come and see, whoever wishes to sanctify himself with the will of his Master should not have marital relations except from midnight onward, or at midnight itself, for at that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in the Garden of Eden, and supernal holiness is aroused, and then is the time to be sanctified - this is for the rest of people; but Torah scholars, who know the ways of Torah, their time is at midnight to rise and labor in Torah, to be joined with the Community of Israel, to praise the holy Name, the holy King. On the night of the Sabbath, when the will of all is found, their union is at that hour, to bring forth the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, as it is said, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - and these are called holy, as it is written (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I the LORD am holy," and it is written (Psalms 1:3), "and he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:41: Behold, it is explained in this teaching that the time of union for the rest of the people on weekdays, which is at midnight, is the time of the sanctification of the Torah scholars in the union of the Community of Israel, by rising to occupy themselves with Torah - and it follows that he is sanctified through a spiritual and holy union in what the rest of the people are sanctified through a physical union. However, on the night of Sabbath, when the Community of Israel is united above and does not need the arousal of Torah from the souls of the righteous - and this is what he said, "when the will of all is found," meaning that of itself a will is found above and it does not need us - then "their union is at that hour, to bring forth the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel," and so on, because the union on the night of Sabbath is in Atzilut, unlike the six weekdays, when the union is below, in Metatron.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:42: And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 93), in these words: and on the Sabbath, which is the seventh day, there is the closeness and unification of the Name YHVH and likewise the sefirot, and therefore Torah scholars have their union from Sabbath night to Sabbath night - these forbidden relations [being permitted only then] are certainly below; but above it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - and a righteous man who has relations with his wife on weekdays, that son that results, of him it is said, "a righteous man to whom it goes badly," for he causes the holy to become profane, which is the seventh day, and at that time it is the secret of "a righteous man to whom it goes badly" - to this point. And what he says concerning "a righteous man who has relations with his wife," and so on, we must say that this righteous man has a soul of Atzilut, which is holy, and therefore causes the holy to become profane - but if he has a soul of Metatron, which is profane, it is profane with profane and is not a blemish, and this is the union of the rest of the people, which is at midnight during the six weekdays, as explained above, because their soul is from there.
